\subsubsection{The transimpedance loop}\label{sss:tia-loop}

The loop that closes around the electrode is characterised in
Tables~\ref{tab:tia-cl-stability} and~\ref{tab:tia-cl-transfer}. At maximum gain, with
the cell model of Figure~\ref{fig:randles-cell} and a \SI{22}{\pico\farad} feedback
capacitor, it holds \SIrange{61.2}{64.9}{\degree} of phase margin and
\SIrange{1.2}{1.5}{\decibel} of peaking across five process corners.

\paragraph{Feedback factor.} Writing $Z_{\mathrm{in}}$ for the impedance from the
summing node to AC ground, the noise gain is $1/\beta = 1 + R_f/Z_{\mathrm{in}}$. For
the cell of Figure~\ref{fig:randles-cell},

\begin{equation}\label{eq:tia-beta}
  Z_{\mathrm{in}}(s) = R_s + \left( R_{\mathrm{ct}} \parallel \frac{1}{sC_{\mathrm{dl}}} \right),
  \qquad
  \frac{1}{\beta} \longrightarrow 1 + \frac{R_f}{R_s}
  \quad \text{for } f \gg \frac{1}{2\pi R_s C_{\mathrm{dl}}} .
\end{equation}

The noise gain is therefore bounded by the solution resistance, and the loop closes at
\SI{20}{\decibel} per decade above $1/2\pi R_s C_{\mathrm{dl}}$.

\paragraph{Electrode dependence.} Phase margin over the declared electrode range, with
no feedback capacitor:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{llcc}
\toprule
$C_{\mathrm{dl}}$ & $R_s$ & $\beta$ zero & Phase margin, $R_f = \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}$ \\
\midrule
\SI{100}{\nano\farad} & \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}  & \SI{1.6}{\kilo\hertz}  & \SIrange{89.8}{90.6}{\degree} \\
\SI{100}{\nano\farad} & \SI{100}{\ohm}     & \SI{15.9}{\kilo\hertz} & \SIrange{35.7}{40.3}{\degree} \\
\SI{1}{\micro\farad}  & both               & --                     & $\geq \SI{90}{\degree}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\SI{22}{\pico\farad} across $R_f$ holds every combination of
$R_s \in \{\SI{100}{\ohm},\ \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}\}$,
$C_{\mathrm{dl}} \in \{\SI{100}{\nano\farad},\ \SI{1}{\micro\farad}\}$ and
$R_f \in \{\SI{35}{\kilo\ohm},\ \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}\}$ above \SI{61}{\degree}, at
approximately \SI{0.011}{\milli\metre\squared} per channel. Peaking meets
\SI{2}{\decibel} at \SI{22}{\pico\farad}; at \SI{5}{\pico\farad} and
\SI{10}{\pico\farad} it is \SIrange{2.3}{3.7}{\decibel}.

Input-referred current noise over \SIrange{0.1}{100}{\hertz} is
\SI{0.48}{\nano\ampere} at $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$ and
\SIrange{2.2}{2.4}{\nano\ampere} at \SI{1}{\micro\farad}.

\paragraph{Charge-transfer resistance.} DC loop gain and the quantities that follow from
it depend on $R_{\mathrm{ct}}$, which sets $\beta$ at DC:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
$R_{\mathrm{ct}}$ & DC loop gain & Gain error & Input offset \\
\midrule
\SI{1}{\mega\ohm}   & \SIrange{76.5}{78.0}{\decibel} & \SI{-0.02}{\percent}                & \SIrange{-0.28}{-0.13}{\milli\volt} \\
\SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}  & \SIrange{41.9}{44.3}{\decibel} & \SIrange{-1.24}{-0.98}{\percent}    & \SIrange{-9.9}{-4.1}{\milli\volt}   \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

At $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}$ the electrode shunts the summing node,
$\beta_{\mathrm{DC}} = \SI{10.1}{\kilo\ohm}/\SI{570}{\kilo\ohm}$, and integral
non-linearity after gain and offset are fitted out is \SIrange{1.27}{1.65}{} LSB.

\paragraph{Conditions.} Five process corners at \SI{25}{\celsius}, schematic-level with
no extracted parasitics, with an ideal feedback resistor in place of the 16-tap string.
